title: Depth Anything V2
mechanism: Scale up the teacher, then train students only on large sets of pseudo-labelled real images, so students learn from a consistent target instead of noisy real labels.
adaptation: Teacher = best heavy model (VFM or ensemble). Students train on 159k pseudo-labelled cells only, with no jittered GT, then get a short PF fine-tune on the 478 cells. Tests whether one consistent crack convention raises relF1@2 and E1 detection.
min_experiment: Arm pseudo-only student (+ short fine-tune) vs house PF, 3 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2 (strict IoU may fall because of per-source conventions). Kill if relF1@2 is n.d. on both sets.
evidence: R: models from 25M to 1.3B parameters; students trained on large pseudo-labelled real sets reported to give finer and more robust predictions than V1 (abstract-level claim; tables not read).
prior_overlap: Not tested; the 159k pool was never used. Open.
